editorial:
Imagine jumping from one colorful planet to another in a race against time. You get to follow Mario and Luigi as they leave the Mushroom Kingdom behind to explore the deep reaches of space. This time around, the threat comes from Bowser Jr., who is a sassy little villain trying to save his dad and take over the galaxy. The whole vibe is bright, loud, and full of energy, making you feel like you are playing a video game from your couch. It is a wild ride that keeps the family dynamic at the center, showing how much the brothers really care for each other while they deal with gravity-defying puzzles.

What really hits home is how the animation looks almost too good to be true. The action scenes are fast, and the jokes land perfectly without feeling forced. While the plot is pretty simple, it never feels boring because the scenery changes every ten minutes. You should definitely watch this if you want something feel-good for the whole family. To get the most out of those glowing star effects, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection so you can see every detail.
endingExplained: In the final battle, Mario and Luigi team up with Rosalina to stop Bowser Jr. from using a giant star power machine. The twist happens when Bowser Jr. realizes his dad actually prefers being a prisoner over dealing with his kid's chaos. They eventually stop the machine, sending the villains flying back to their own realm. Everyone returns home safely, and the brothers celebrate with a huge party in the Mushroom Kingdom.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Nintendo games and fun family adventures.
